- [PC Only] Added an option to disable dithering.
- [PSVita Only] Made so that controls scheme work as with a Dualshock controller (Aka true analogs support).
- Added controls rebinding support in the Options menu.
- Fixed a bug causing main menu to get stale texts after AdHoc matches.
- Fixed a bug causing the mask grab animation to break in Hot Air Skywat under certain circumstances.
- Added the possibility to locally save ghosts from the Online Leaderboard.
- Added the possibility to challenge ghosts from the Ghost Replay end screen.
- Made so that the powerslide bar changes color dynamically instead of being only two distinct sections.
- [PSVita Only] Improved performances in Tiger Temple by optimizing the flame spit by the statues.
- Added Tiger Temple Alternative in the map pool for Relic Race and Time Trial.
- [PC Only] Fixed a bug causing some controllers (eg. DualSense) to be detected as two controllers.
- Moved all the gameplay cheatcodes in a dedicated submenu in Options. Cheats will also now be saved and kept between game sessions.

- Fixed the speedometer having wrong scale.
- Fixed a bug causing some menu entries to be partially offscreen in certain languages.
- Fixed a lot of animations being at wrong speed when playing in 60 FPS.
- Adjusted physics at 60 FPS to more closely match 30 FPS mode. (This fixes the R in Hot Sky Airway during the CTR Challenge to be impossible to reach amongst other things)

- Added personal bests showcase (for both 1L and 3L) during Time Trials.
- Made so that current laps during a Time Trial change color based on how close you are to your personal best.
- Added custom characters support (Check the "How to add new custom characters to the game" for more info).
- Added a new option that allows to enable custom characters for enemy AIs in Arcade mode (Single and Cup).

v0.1 2026-09-13 20:59 UTC
# N.O.V.A. 3 Vita v0.1

The first public release of N.O.V.A. 3 for PS Vita.

Campaign gameplay works on real Vita hardware, with dual-analog controls, front touch, audio, combat, full ragdolls, checkpoints and level transitions. The current quality-focused setup uses a maximum of 30 FPS.

## What you need

Download `NOVA3Vita_v0.1.vpk` and the Windows data helper from the [GitLab Releases page](https://gitlab.com/sexcurrybeats/nova3-vita/-/releases). Supply your own legally obtained exact Android **1.0.7** APK, main OBB and patch OBB, prepare the data, then install the VPK with VitaShell.

The VPK and source include launcher presentation artwork, but no APK, OBBs, original game library or gameplay data. Building from source is optional. Follow [Installing](https://gitlab.com/sexcurrybeats/nova3-vita/-/blob/v0.1/docs/INSTALLING.md) for setup.

## Known issues

- Campaign loading and mid-level transitions are slow.
- Heavier fights can hitch; performance is not locked to 30 FPS.
- Later levels, full-game stability, slow-time controls and LAN multiplayer have not been fully tested. Original internet services are unsupported.

This is an early release. See the [README](https://gitlab.com/sexcurrybeats/nova3-vita/-/blob/v0.1/README.md) for controls and the full list of limitations.

The bundled preparation helper is Windows-only. macOS preparation has not been validated for this release. Existing development installations may retain a default LiveArea; see the installation notes.

### New
- Added support for [Adrenaline 8.0.2](https://github.com/isage/Adrenaline/releases/tag/v8.0.2) by Isage.
- Added support for DAX and ZSO PSP game file formats when using Adrenaline 8.
- Added the ability to toggle the visibility of individual categories and collections. (Settings > Categories).

### Improvements
- Improved performance when hiding games, editing overrides, and creating new collections, with less reliance on full cache reloads.
- Updated bundled Adrenaline Bubble Booter module sets. RetroFlow now uses [AdrBubbleBooter-oss](https://github.com/shoui520/AdrBubbleBooter-oss) by shoui520.
- The 'Edit collections' setting has moved from 'Other settings' to 'Settings > Categories'.

### Bug fixes
- Individual background images weren't downloading when "Download using CRC" was turned off.
- Vectrex games were being added to the Sega Master System category.

### Migrated Adrenaline drivers
- If you have saved Adrenaline overrides, the driver names displayed for your saved overrides may change. This is expected because older versions of Adrenaline Bubble Booter used incorrect driver labels. Your existing driver selections have been migrated, so games should continue to behave as before.

### Installation
- Please read and follow the [installation and setup guide](https://github.com/jimbob4000/RetroFlow-Launcher#installation--setup).

### Downgrading
If you need to downgrade from RetroFlow 8.4.0 to an earlier version, please follow these steps.

1. Delete the 'RetroFlow Adrenaline Launcher' bubble.
2. Replace the `ux0:/data/RetroFlow/launch_overrides.lua` file with the `launch_overrides_before_abm_driver_fix.lua` file in the same directory if the file is available.
3. Uninstall the Adrenaline Bubble Booter modules, see the FAQ here for [how to uninstall Adrenaline Bubble Booter](https://github.com/jimbob4000/RetroFlow-Launcher/blob/main/docs/FAQs.md#how-do-i-uninstall-adrenaline-bubble-booter).

### Help and FAQs
- Please see the [FAQs](https://github.com/jimbob4000/RetroFlow-Launcher/blob/main/docs/FAQs.md) page.

### Nightly build
- See the [nightly build](https://github.com/jimbob4000/RetroFlow-Launcher/releases/tag/Nightly) for a preview of new features and bug fixes.

<br>

**Note:** This release was AI-assisted.

# Public Release v0.73

This is the biggest **DeltaruneVita** update to date, focused on texture memory, Room transitions, native video/audio, loading screens, patchers, language support, Chapter 3/5 performance, and overall Vita stability.

v0.73 consolidates the work developed throughout the internal **v0.70**, **v0.71**, and **v0.72** builds into a new public release.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> This update requires generating and transferring a **fresh data folder using a v0.73 patcher**.
>
> The rebuilt `data.win`, BC3/RGBA4444 caches, language data, and patch manifests must all come from the same v0.73 preparation pipeline.
>
> **Do not reuse or mix caches generated for older Texture Page layouts.**

## Main Changes

### Loading screen

The loading and texture-generation presentation has been substantially redesigned.

<p align="center"><em>Texture generation screen with the optional loading mini-game.</em></p>

- Added localized loading/generation labels and real texture/shader progress.
- Added multiple Toby loading animations.

<p align="center">
<img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/WolffsRoom/DeltaruneVita/gh-pages/assets/screenshots/v0.73/toby-loading/toby_walk.gif" alt="Toby walk loading animation" width="80">

- Added a loading animation that follows the progress bar and accelerates off-screen once texture preparation is complete:

<img width="20" height="42" alt="frame_0" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c0b57ac6-ce12-456b-9b57-70aeaeaad52a" />

### Optional texture-generation mini-game

- Added an optional full-screen mini-game during **GENERATING TEXTURES**.
- The optional loading mini-game recreates DELTARUNE's battle-defense phase, allowing you to move the Heart and dodge enemy-style attack patterns while textures are being generated.

The mini-game is optional. If it is never activated, the normal texture-generation path remains synchronous.

When PLAY is enabled during generation, the current texture page is completed safely before the remaining preparation work is handed to the background worker. VitaGL rendering remains on the main thread.

### Textures: DeltaRepack and DeltaCache

v0.73 consolidates the new texture pipeline developed after v0.69.

The preparation flow is now:

```text
Official DELTARUNE data.win
↓
DeltaRepack
(room-aware Texture Page rebuild)
↓
Final rebuilt data.win
↓
DeltaCache
(validated BC3 + RGBA4444 caches)
↓
PS Vita runtime
```

- **[DeltaRepack](https://github.com/WolffsRoom/DeltaRepack/)** rebuilds GameMaker Texture Pages into a more granular layout designed to reduce the amount of unrelated texture data kept resident by a Room.
- Large sparse atlases can be replaced with smaller or rectangular power-of-two layouts where appropriate.
- **[DeltaCache](https://github.com/WolffsRoom/DeltaCache/)** generates GPU-ready `.bc3.pvr` and `.r444` files from the final rebuilt `data.win`.
- Generated caches are validated against the final TXTR metadata before being accepted.
- Font, textbox, and other pixel-critical Texture Pages remain on the safer lossless-compatible path.
- BC3/DXT5 is used where its memory savings are beneficial without sacrificing critical UI/text quality.
- Missing eligible caches can be generated locally on the Vita during **GENERATING TEXTURES**.
- Complete cache sets use fast completion markers instead of rescanning every texture file at every startup.
- Language packs keep their own matching cache layouts when their `data.win` changes atlas contents or indices.

The higher rebuilt Texture Page count is intentional: smaller pages allow the runtime to keep a more focused per-Room working set instead of keeping a few oversized atlases resident.

### Room-aware texture residency and memory

<p align="center">
<img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/WolffsRoom/DeltaruneVita/gh-pages/assets/screenshots/v0.73/texture/Graphics.png" alt="DeltaruneVita graphics settings" width="49%">
<img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/WolffsRoom/DeltaruneVita/gh-pages/assets/screenshots/v0.73/texture/Texture.png" alt="DeltaruneVita texture settings" width="49%">
</p>

<p align="center"><em>Graphics and texture-memory configuration used by the optimized Vita pipeline.</em></p>

Texture residency, preload, and eviction behavior received extensive work across Chapters 2–5.

- Improved Room-aware texture residency and eviction.
- Reduced repeated uploads of stale Texture Pages during transitions.
- Improved handling of current-Room and near-Room resources.
- Added safer memory policies for particularly heavy Chapter 3 and Chapter 5 sequences.
- Protected font/UI pages from inappropriate BC3 compression.
- Improved transition-time cleanup so stale textures can be retired before destination-Room uploads.
- Reduced unnecessary retained CPU-side texture staging in memory-heavy Chapters.
- Improved prepared-texture validation and fallback handling.
- Expanded semantic resource detection so important assets are increasingly tracked by their real GameMaker resources instead of hardcoded Texture Page IDs.
- Fixed dynamic Texture Page tracking when new textures are created from surfaces, preventing renderer bookkeeping corruption after runtime page growth.

### Native video playback

The native video work from v0.72 is now part of the v0.73 public release.

<img src="https://media.tenor.com/42LC_etFIIcAAAAj/deltarune-tenna.gif" alt="Tenna Dance" width="200" align="left" hspace="0">

- Added the native `SceAvPlayer` backend for GameMaker video functions (no FFmpeg/libavcodec or external Vita video plugin is required).
- Implemented Vita paths for `video_open`, `video_draw`, `video_close`, status, position, duration, looping, and volume.
- Added GameMaker-compatible `video_start` / `video_end` async event handling.
- Video frames are decoded by SceAvPlayer and presented through VitaGL/SceGxm.
- Chapter 3 retains the original GameMaker subtitle/event lifecycle around native video playback.
- Added safer CPU/PHYCONT cleanup after video playback.

<br>

#### Safer video shutdown

The SceAvPlayer teardown path was revised after investigation of a post-video Vita crash.

The Vita video-audio worker is now stopped and joined before the AVPlayer controller is destroyed:

```text
Video state -> INACTIVE
↓
Audio worker exits
↓
Thread joined
↓
sceAvPlayerStop()
↓
sceAvPlayerClose()
```

This prevents the video-audio worker from accessing an AVPlayer object while it is being destroyed.

### Audio

Audio handling has received major transition and streaming improvements.

<img src="https://i.redd.it/mixcj0cg2k6d1.gif" alt="Cup and cakes" width="170" align="left" hspace="0">

- Music playback across Room transitions has been improved to preserve compatible streams and playback positions whenever possible. Transitions are now smoother when the destination Room changes music, reducing unnecessary restarts, repeated track intros, and audio issues during long Room or texture-loading stalls.
- Several fixes were also made to the streaming backend, including corrected stale OpenAL buffer handling, proper seeking for streamed OGG audio, and earlier audio initialization for Vita runtime paths that depend on it.
- Native video playback now uses a dedicated Vita audio path, preventing it from disrupting the game's normal OpenAL output. Loading and mini-game sounds also use dedicated OpenAL sources, allowing them to play even while normal startup audio is intentionally held.
- Frequently used battle SFX can now be prepared earlier, reducing first-use stalls during gameplay.

<br>
<br>
<br>

### Battle dialogue rendering

The battle-dialogue clipping issue reported in previous public builds has received a renderer-side fix.

- Fixed the final pixel row of some `fnt_main` glyphs being clipped in battle dialogue.
- The issue was caused by VitaGL rasterization at the glyph quad boundary, not by missing font pixels in `data.win` or the generated texture cache.
- v0.73 preserves DELTARUNE's original line spacing and font layout.
- The renderer explicitly restores the real final texel row only for the affected battle-text path.
- The fix applies globally to Chapters that use the same battle writer/font path instead of being hardcoded to Chapter 2 or 3.

### Game Settings

The Vita-native Game Settings menu continues to expand.

<p align="center">
<img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/WolffsRoom/DeltaruneVita/gh-pages/assets/screenshots/v0.73/GraphicSettings.png" alt="DeltaruneVita v0.73 graphics settings" width="900">
</p>

<p align="center"><em>Vita-native graphics and performance settings.</em></p>

Open it with **Select**.

Available options include:

- Native / Balanced / Performance resolution profiles.
- Optimized / None / Aggressive texture-compression modes.
- 30 / 40 / 60 FPS and unlocked frame-rate modes.
- **Legacy GL** and experimental **Modern GL** renderer selection.
- Scanlines, Sharp Bilinear, Dithering, and VHS screen effects.
- Dynamic / Simple / Disabled console borders.
- Master / Music / SFX volume controls.
- Touch-control configuration.
- Language selection.
- Trophy and notification settings.
- Developer diagnostics and Room tools when Dev Mode is enabled.

Recommended settings:

```text
Resolution: Native
Texture compression: Optimized
Frame-rate limit: 30 FPS
Renderer: Legacy GL
```

Legacy GL remains the recommended renderer for normal gameplay.

## Updating from v0.69, internal v0.70–v0.72 builds, or older versions

1. Install `Deltarune-v0.73.vpk`.
2. Generate a fresh data folder using either v0.73 patcher (Deltarune Vita Patcher or Seam's Patcher).
3. Replace the older generated `deltarune` data with the v0.73 output.
4. Do not mix old Texture Page caches with the new rebuilt `data.win`.

## Known Issues

- **Modern GL remains experimental** and may produce missing graphics, shader problems, or GPU instability.
- Chapter 3's heaviest TV/battle sequences can still show performance drops or first-use stalls.
- Chapter 5 remains the most demanding chapter and can still encounter low FPS or memory pressure in complex scenes and battles.
- Some Chapter 5 shadow/effect behavior is not yet fully reproduced by the Legacy GL renderer.
- 60 FPS compatibility continues to improve, but **30 FPS remains the recommended default**.
- Some first-use textures or sound effects may still cause a short hitch in demanding sequences.
- Translation packages whose Texture Page layout differs from the original game require their matching v0.73 caches.

# Public Release v0.73

This is the biggest **DeltaruneVita** update to date, focused on texture memory, Room transitions, native video/audio, loading screens, patchers, language support, Chapter 3/5 performance, and overall Vita stability.

v0.73 consolidates the work developed throughout the internal **v0.70**, **v0.71**, and **v0.72** builds into a new public release.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> This update requires generating and transferring a **fresh data folder using a v0.73 patcher**.
>
> The rebuilt `data.win`, BC3/RGBA4444 caches, language data, and patch manifests must all come from the same v0.73 preparation pipeline.
>
> **Do not reuse or mix caches generated for older Texture Page layouts.**

### Optional texture-generation mini-game

- Added an optional full-screen mini-game during **GENERATING TEXTURES**.
- The optional loading mini-game recreates DELTARUNE's battle-defense phase, allowing you to move the Heart and dodge enemy-style attack patterns while textures are being generated.

The mini-game is optional. If it is never activated, the normal texture-generation path remains synchronous.

When PLAY is enabled during generation, the current texture page is completed safely before the remaining preparation work is handed to the background worker. VitaGL rendering remains on the main thread.

### Textures: DeltaRepack and DeltaCache

v0.73 consolidates the new texture pipeline developed after v0.69.

The preparation flow is now:

```text
Official DELTARUNE data.win
↓
DeltaRepack
(room-aware Texture Page rebuild)
↓
Final rebuilt data.win
↓
DeltaCache
(validated BC3 + RGBA4444 caches)
↓
PS Vita runtime
```

- **[DeltaRepack](https://github.com/WolffsRoom/DeltaRepack/)** rebuilds GameMaker Texture Pages into a more granular layout designed to reduce the amount of unrelated texture data kept resident by a Room.
- Large sparse atlases can be replaced with smaller or rectangular power-of-two layouts where appropriate.
- **[DeltaCache](https://github.com/WolffsRoom/DeltaCache/)** generates GPU-ready `.bc3.pvr` and `.r444` files from the final rebuilt `data.win`.
- Generated caches are validated against the final TXTR metadata before being accepted.
- Font, textbox, and other pixel-critical Texture Pages remain on the safer lossless-compatible path.
- BC3/DXT5 is used where its memory savings are beneficial without sacrificing critical UI/text quality.
- Missing eligible caches can be generated locally on the Vita during **GENERATING TEXTURES**.
- Complete cache sets use fast completion markers instead of rescanning every texture file at every startup.
- Language packs keep their own matching cache layouts when their `data.win` changes atlas contents or indices.

The higher rebuilt Texture Page count is intentional: smaller pages allow the runtime to keep a more focused per-Room working set instead of keeping a few oversized atlases resident.

### Room-aware texture residency and memory

<p align="center">
<img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/WolffsRoom/DeltaruneVita/gh-pages/assets/screenshots/v0.73/texture/Graphics.png" alt="DeltaruneVita graphics settings" width="49%">
<img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/WolffsRoom/DeltaruneVita/gh-pages/assets/screenshots/v0.73/texture/Texture.png" alt="DeltaruneVita texture settings" width="49%">
</p>

<p align="center"><em>Graphics and texture-memory configuration used by the optimized Vita pipeline.</em></p>

Texture residency, preload, and eviction behavior received extensive work across Chapters 2–5.

- Improved Room-aware texture residency and eviction.
- Reduced repeated uploads of stale Texture Pages during transitions.
- Improved handling of current-Room and near-Room resources.
- Added safer memory policies for particularly heavy Chapter 3 and Chapter 5 sequences.
- Protected font/UI pages from inappropriate BC3 compression.
- Improved transition-time cleanup so stale textures can be retired before destination-Room uploads.
- Reduced unnecessary retained CPU-side texture staging in memory-heavy Chapters.
- Improved prepared-texture validation and fallback handling.
- Expanded semantic resource detection so important assets are increasingly tracked by their real GameMaker resources instead of hardcoded Texture Page IDs.
- Fixed dynamic Texture Page tracking when new textures are created from surfaces, preventing renderer bookkeeping corruption after runtime page growth.

### Native video playback

The native video work from v0.72 is now part of the v0.73 public release.

<img src="https://media.tenor.com/42LC_etFIIcAAAAj/deltarune-tenna.gif" alt="Tenna Dance" width="200" align="left" hspace="0">

- Added the native `SceAvPlayer` backend for GameMaker video functions (no FFmpeg/libavcodec or external Vita video plugin is required).
- Implemented Vita paths for `video_open`, `video_draw`, `video_close`, status, position, duration, looping, and volume.
- Added GameMaker-compatible `video_start` / `video_end` async event handling.
- Video frames are decoded by SceAvPlayer and presented through VitaGL/SceGxm.
- Chapter 3 retains the original GameMaker subtitle/event lifecycle around native video playback.
- Added safer CPU/PHYCONT cleanup after video playback.

<br>

#### Safer video shutdown

The SceAvPlayer teardown path was revised after investigation of a post-video Vita crash.

The Vita video-audio worker is now stopped and joined before the AVPlayer controller is destroyed:

```text
Video state -> INACTIVE
↓
Audio worker exits
↓
Thread joined
↓
sceAvPlayerStop()
↓
sceAvPlayerClose()
```

This prevents the video-audio worker from accessing an AVPlayer object while it is being destroyed.

### Audio

Audio handling has received major transition and streaming improvements.

<img src="https://i.redd.it/mixcj0cg2k6d1.gif" alt="Cup and cakes" width="170" align="left" hspace="0">

- Music playback across Room transitions has been improved to preserve compatible streams and playback positions whenever possible. Transitions are now smoother when the destination Room changes music, reducing unnecessary restarts, repeated track intros, and audio issues during long Room or texture-loading stalls.
- Several fixes were also made to the streaming backend, including corrected stale OpenAL buffer handling, proper seeking for streamed OGG audio, and earlier audio initialization for Vita runtime paths that depend on it.
- Native video playback now uses a dedicated Vita audio path, preventing it from disrupting the game's normal OpenAL output. Loading and mini-game sounds also use dedicated OpenAL sources, allowing them to play even while normal startup audio is intentionally held.
- Frequently used battle SFX can now be prepared earlier, reducing first-use stalls during gameplay.

<br>
<br>
<br>

### Battle dialogue rendering

The battle-dialogue clipping issue reported in previous public builds has received a renderer-side fix.

- Fixed the final pixel row of some `fnt_main` glyphs being clipped in battle dialogue.
- The issue was caused by VitaGL rasterization at the glyph quad boundary, not by missing font pixels in `data.win` or the generated texture cache.
- v0.73 preserves DELTARUNE's original line spacing and font layout.
- The renderer explicitly restores the real final texel row only for the affected battle-text path.
- The fix applies globally to Chapters that use the same battle writer/font path instead of being hardcoded to Chapter 2 or 3.

Legacy GL remains the recommended renderer for normal gameplay.

- Continued dynamic console-border improvements.
- Added/corrected Chapter 3 border mappings for TV, game-show, Castle Town, and special Rooms.
- Improved border behavior during Room transitions.
- Fixed Chapter 3 game-show presentation regressions introduced during texture-memory experimentation.
- Continued fixes for missing/flashing assets caused by aggressive memory pressure.
- Improved pixel-critical texture handling for UI and fonts.

### Runtime and stability

- Continued Chapter 3 and Chapter 5 memory-pressure work.
- Improved renderer behavior around heavy surface usage.
- Added safer dynamic texture tracking.
- Improved Room transition cleanup.
- Reduced repeated Texture Page loading in several high-pressure sequences.
- Added protections around native-video teardown.
- Improved diagnostics for memory, textures, video, and audio.
- Continued compatibility fixes for GameMaker behavior required by Chapters 1–5.
- Preserved save data separately under `ux0:data/deltarune_saves/`.

## Chapter Compatibility and Performance Notes

<details>
<summary><strong>Chapter 1</strong></summary>

- Playable and extensively reviewed.
- Additional first-use battle resource preparation.
- Improved music continuity across Room transitions.
- Reduced unnecessary audio restart behavior.
- Continues to serve as one of the most stable chapters in the port.

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>Chapter 2</strong></summary>

- Playable.
- Retains the previous fixes for light puzzles, mice sequences, battles, texture residency, and Room transitions.
- Improved castle/city/mansion memory behavior.
- Improved battle dialogue rendering.
- Additional audio-transition and texture-cache work.

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>Chapter 3</strong></summary>

Chapter 3 received the largest amount of v0.73-specific development work.

- Native MP4 playback.
- Chapter 3 Tenna video integration.
- Original GameMaker async video lifecycle support.
- Improved TV/game-show texture memory behavior.
- Additional Room-transition profiling and cleanup.
- Game-show visual fixes.
- Rhythm / mini-game resource preparation.
- Border corrections.
- Reduced unnecessary RGBA4444 residency in heavy presentation sequences.
- Continued investigation of demanding battle and TV Rooms.

Chapter 3 remains one of the main performance-testing targets.

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>Chapter 4</strong></summary>

- Playable.
- Uses the rebuilt Texture Page layout and matching caches.
- Improved runtime/interface compatibility.
- Fixed dynamic Texture Page bookkeeping after runtime surface/sprite creation.
- Language-specific cache layouts remain supported.

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>Chapter 5</strong></summary>

- Playable.
- Continues to benefit heavily from the rebuilt texture pipeline.
- Improved Room-aware cleanup and texture residency.
- Reduced memory pressure in heavy battles and composition sequences.
- More aggressive compression can be used for non-critical pages while fonts/UI remain protected.
- Chapter 5 remains the largest overall memory/performance stress test.

</details>

## Updating from v0.69, internal v0.70–v0.72 builds, or older versions

1. Install `Deltarune-v0.73.vpk`.
2. Generate a fresh data folder using either v0.73 patcher (Deltarune Vita Patcher or Seam's Patcher).
3. Replace the older generated `deltarune` data with the v0.73 output.
4. Do not mix old Texture Page caches with the new rebuilt `data.win`.

## Known Issues

- **Modern GL remains experimental** and may produce missing graphics, shader problems, or GPU instability.
- Chapter 3's heaviest TV/battle sequences can still show performance drops or first-use stalls.
- Chapter 5 remains the most demanding chapter and can still encounter low FPS or memory pressure in complex scenes and battles.
- Some Chapter 5 shadow/effect behavior is not yet fully reproduced by the Legacy GL renderer.
- 60 FPS compatibility continues to improve, but **30 FPS remains the recommended default**.
- Some first-use textures or sound effects may still cause a short hitch in demanding sequences.
- Translation packages whose Texture Page layout differs from the original game require their matching v0.73 caches.

For full setup steps, please refer to the [Installation Guide](https://github.com/WolffsRoom/DeltaruneVita#installation-guide).

If you encounter a problem, please open a ticket on the Issues page:

https://github.com/WolffsRoom/DeltaruneVita/issues

Please include:

```text
ux0:data/deltarune/deltarunevita/butterscotch-probe.log
```

and, when relevant:

- Chapter and Room.
- Selected language.
- Renderer.
- Texture-compression mode.
- FPS limit.
- Screenshot/video of visual problems.
- Generated `psp2dmp` crash dump when available.

If Dev Mode is enabled, also include the corresponding diagnostic information from the affected Room.

# Plants vs. Zombies 2 for PS Vita — 1.1 RC12

RC12 fixes reproduced texture upload and allocation-recovery defects:

- Correct mip handling for resized textures and placeholders.
- Consistent RGBA8 storage and conversion for packed 4444/565 texture updates.
- Checked recovery after failed alpha uploads or CPU downsampling.
- Avoids retrying a larger allocation after a smaller one already failed.
- Reports unrecoverable graphics-memory failure instead of continuing with
resized render targets or failed placeholder storage.

Install `pvz2-vita-latest.vpk` over the existing version. Keep your game files
and `userdata/`; no game data replacement is required.

Six regression cases fail against RC11 and pass against RC12. Compiled ARM
checks verify the storage/update pixel bytes and the prior timezone fix;
shader lifetime and pixel-worker checks also pass. No Vita3K was used.

The new RC11 log contains four texture allocation errors and reaches 189600
frames. Both supplied crash dumps are duplicates of older timezone crashes.
**These fixes are verified in isolated tests, but the reported latest crash
is not conclusively identified and RC12 hardware confirmation is pending.**
Placeholder recovery may omit artwork. If graphics allocation cannot recover,
the app reports an error and must be relaunched. Busy-scene FPS drops remain.

For a recurring crash, retain the newly generated dump and
`ux0:data/pvz2/userdata/loader.log` before relaunching, plus `stall.log` if present.
Include the build ID and the world/level/menu action.

Asphalt 8 Vita v0.3

v0.3 2026-09-11 02:10 UTC
# Asphalt 8 Vita v0.3

This update improves race loading, reduces shader-related pauses and adds
further stability and compatibility fixes.
Your existing game files, saves and settings remain compatible.

### Improvements

- **Fewer shader-related pauses.** Bundled shader programs cover shared track
and vehicle effects from their first use, with broader coverage for equivalent
variants used throughout the game.
- **More reliable shader reuse.** Fixed a cache-length issue that could cause a
complete cached program to be rejected and compiled again.
- **Faster race loading.** Race loading shares the OBB directory data
between active scans instead of repeatedly reading the same large directory.
- **Loading recovery.** Added targeted recovery for a stalled loading stage
that could prevent the game from finishing a load after time spent idle.
- **Audio compatibility.** Improved PCM sample-rate handling and read-only Vox
state queries, avoiding unnecessary waits in those queries.
- **Further session-stability fixes.** Improved cleanup of the game's thread
synchronization objects when their memory is freed, and synchronized shader
program deletion with outstanding GPU work.
- **Broader shader compatibility.** Improved handling of shaders that exceed
the usual varying slots, plus validation and serialization of cached programs.
- **Clearer setup errors.** An APK size mismatch now names the supported
v2.0.0e APK instead of referring to an internal development build.
- **Updated presentation.** Includes the new bubble icon and LiveArea artwork.
- **Easier Windows setup.** File pickers and a guided USB or PC-folder option
handle file preparation and verification. FTP remains available.

The update retains traffic, breakables, collision behavior, car damage,
particles and the existing graphics presets.

The recurring in-race pauses improved in Tokyo, Iceland and Nevada testing.
Bundled programs cover their matching effects on first use, including the
first run of a new installation. Effects outside that coverage still use the
normal shader compiler; this is not a promise of hitch-free play on every track.

### Updating

Install the new VPK over your existing installation. Keep your game-data folder
and saves; there is no need to copy the APK/OBB again or clear the shader cache.

### Known issues

- The pause when finishing a race remains
- Heavy scenes can still slow down; 60 FPS and hitch-free play are not guaranteed
- Premium-currency cars, car packs, online services and gyro steering remain
unavailable
- Only the exact supported Android v2.0.0e game files are supported

## Downloads

- **[Install package](https://gitlab.com/sexcurrybeats/asphalt8-vita/-/releases/v0.3/downloads/Asphalt8Vita_v0.3.zip)** — playable VPK, guided Windows setup, and instructions.
- [Source ZIP](https://gitlab.com/sexcurrybeats/asphalt8-vita/-/releases/v0.3/downloads/asphalt8-vita-v0.3-source.zip) — source snapshot with its integrity manifest. Building is optional.
- [SHA-256 checksums](https://gitlab.com/sexcurrybeats/asphalt8-vita/-/releases/v0.3/downloads/SHA256SUMS.txt).

Supply your own exact supported v2.0.0e APK and OBB. See [installation instructions](https://gitlab.com/sexcurrybeats/asphalt8-vita/-/blob/v0.3/docs/INSTALL.md), [compatibility](https://gitlab.com/sexcurrybeats/asphalt8-vita/-/blob/v0.3/docs/COMPATIBILITY.md), and [shader provenance](https://gitlab.com/sexcurrybeats/asphalt8-vita/-/blob/v0.3/docs/SHADER_PROVENANCE.md).

1.4 2026-09-10 17:51 UTC
## Major UI and Camera Streaming Update

- New Sony PAF interface that is cleaner and easier to read.
- Larger text and controls for better visibility on the PS Vita screen.
- Redesigned streaming mode presentation with distinct colors.
- Added camera streaming with two native resolution profiles:
- **640×480 at 60 FPS**
- **480×272 at 30 FPS**
- Added support for both front and rear cameras, with switching via the **L/R buttons**.
- Added support for the PS Vita microphone during camera streaming.
- Camera streaming now uses native resolutions directly, without resizing.
- Improved compatibility with the Windows Camera app and OBS.
- Improved camera mode stability, especially with the **480×272** profile.
- Improved memory management when switching or stopping streaming modes.
- Camera, microphone, and audio resources are now released when streaming stops.
- Improved USB recovery after streaming errors.
- Screen On and Screen Off modes are now clearly identified.
- In Screen Off mode, disconnecting the USB cable restores the display, while reconnecting it turns the display off again.
- Improved standby and wake-up behavior during streaming.
- The interface now clearly displays the active source: screen, front camera, or rear camera.
- Improved installation, updating, and detection of VitaUSBStream, HomebrewUpdate, and HomebrewPatch.
- Various stability improvements and minor fixes.

Vita RomM v0.8.0.s

v0.8.0.s 2026-09-06 18:50 UTC
## Vita RomM v0.8.0.s

First public test release of Vita RomM.

Vita RomM is a PS Vita homebrew client for browsing a self-hosted RomM library and downloading your own backed-up games directly on the Vita.

### Features

- Browse RomM platforms directly on PS Vita.
- View games with cached cover art.
- Download and install PS Vita game archives.
- Download PSP games for Adrenaline.
- Download PSX `.bin/.cue` sets and PSX EBOOT.PBP games.
- Download common retro ROMs into configured emulator folders.
- Show downloaded/installed status where supported.
- Refresh LiveArea from inside the app.
- Refresh cached cover art with `Select`.

### Supported platforms

- PS Vita
- PSP
- PSX / PlayStation
- Game Boy Advance
- Game Boy
- Game Boy Color
- NES
- SNES
- Sega Mega Drive / Genesis
- Nintendo 64 experimental
- Custom RomM platforms with configured paths

### Setup

1. Install `vita_romm.vpk` with VitaShell.
2. Launch Vita RomM once.
3. Edit:
```text
ux0:data/vita-romm/config.txt
```
4. Set your RomM server URL and API token:
server_url=http://your-romm-server.local/
api_token=rmm_your_token_here

See README.md for the full configuration guide.

to squash them" rule
- Fixed a frog telegraph animation desync on late isles, a three-part
lightning lifecycle bug (bolts during death fades, frozen through
hit-stop, popping across pause), and sparse weather at isle start
- weather/difficulty tables moved into the generated level config instead
of hard-coded level indices in the engine - reordering isles can no
longer silently misattach them

### New: difficulty & reward
- Rift-touched eagles (isles 9-10) telegraph a dive attack: a hover-flash
warning, then a fast dive at wherever you're standing
- **FLAWLESS bonus**: clear an isle with every gem and zero damage for
+500 score - now tracked live in the HUD, not just revealed at the door

### New: story
- A short lore beat between each of isles 2-10, setting up what's ahead

### New: visuals
- Hero: a dash streak pose and a hit-recoil tilt
- Enemies: elite auras now breathe instead of a flat glow; bosses go
visibly enraged below 1/3 HP (bigger glow, red fury flicker)
- Environment: haze and god rays now match the isle's weather - cool
moonlight through the firefly hollows, grey overcast in the storm,
molten orange over the embers
- HUD: the dash cooldown pip is labeled

24 automated tests, all 10 isles physics-verified reachable and soak-tested
clean. Code is MIT © Onur Kuru. Art is Ansimuz's CC0 "Sunny Land" packs.

## PSVitaAlive 02.01

Major update since **01.18** — themes, fonts, plugins, installs, UI readability, multilanguage, and stability.

### Highlights
- Full **multilanguage** UI (EN, ES, FR, DE, IT, pt-BR, pt-PT, RU) — System or Manual in Settings
- **Color themes** with first-run picker, preview + confirm, and smooth cross-fade
- **Font styles** selectable in Settings (system PGF)
- **Plugin** catalog links + essential plugin checks (kubridge, fd_fix, libshacccg)
- Safer **NoPspEmuDrm / NoNpDrm** detection (commented lines ≠ installed; no startup crash)
- **PSP/PS1** install paths: LiveArea vs Adrenaline (Folder/ISO), DLC rules clarified
- Larger text, multi-line toasts, catalog tab **app counts**, and many overlay layout fixes

---

### Themes & personalization
- Many distinct color palettes (original **PsVitaAlive**, Vita-inspired, reds, oranges, neutrals, etc.)
- First launch: theme picker (touch + controls, adaptive scroll)
- Settings: open the same picker (no more left/right theme cycling)
- Preview on first select, confirm with second press or **Save**
- Smooth **gradient transition** between themes
- Mono logo/loading assets tinted to the active theme (brand theme keeps original art)

### Fonts
- UI font style option in Settings (system `.pgf` styles with fallback)

### Multilanguage
- Complete EN + ES strings for UI, overlays, toasts, install flow, loading screen
- Additional packs: French, German, Italian, Portuguese (BR/PT), Russian
- Catalog loading / startup update messages localized

### Plugins
- New catalog link type **Plugin** (`type`, `name`, `size`, `extract_path`, `section`, `line`)
- Install: download → path → append line to `tai/config.txt` (no overwrite of existing lines)
- **Install All** installs plugins after VPK / Game Files / Data Files; skips already installed
- Post-install **reboot** modal (soft reset) + L-button boot-loop tip; LiveArea exit blocked until done
- Essential plugins prompt after theme/news if kubridge / fd_fix / libshacccg missing
- Settings **INFO / SYSTEM**: plugin status (OK / missing)
- Validation: file **and** active (non-commented) config line where required

### Downloads, network & TLS
- libcurl / OpenSSL path improvements, retries, clearer SSL diagnostics
- Faster icon/screenshot appearance in typical use
- Anti-suspend / keep screen on during download–install–extract
- Clear lock messages while a job is running
- ZIP/VPK extract **retries** (short delay) for transient E0CD / incomplete reads

### PSP / PS1 / Vita installs
- Adrenaline unpack path (Folder default; ISO option) without breaking Vita VPK/PKG flow
- **PSP DLC** only when LiveArea or Adrenaline **Folder** (ISO blocked with toast)
- LiveArea PSP/PS1 requires **NoPspEmuDrm** (kern + user); toast suggests AutoPlugin II or Adrenaline
- NoPspEmuDrm **no longer** shows a startup toast (still in Settings + install path)

### UI / UX
- Larger fonts across modals, detail, settings INFO, install/progress windows
- Touch hitboxes and settings scroll fixed (no items over header)
- Theme/settings touch scroll aligned with main catalog feel
- Redundant top **DLC** badge removed (bottom chip only)
- Active catalog tab shows **count** e.g. `PSP (total)` (filtered list when searching)
- Multi-line **toasts** with larger text and longer duration for important hints
- Marquee on overflowing labels (e.g. select-links)

### Stability
- Startup crash when NoPspEmuDrm lines missing/commented: fixed (deferred plugin toasts + safer detector)
- Settings crash related to new config fields: fixed
- Build fixes (ternary/`L()`, soft reset API, pkg2zip CRC symbol clash, etc.)

### Recommendations
- **ITLS-ENSO** (full) recommended for HTTPS: https://github.com/SKGleba/iTLS-Enso
- Keep NoNpDrm (and NoPspEmuDrm if you use LiveArea PSP/PS1)
- During large downloads, leave the app in foreground; screen is kept awake while busy

# VagaChatVITA Alpha 0.1.0

Primera versión alpha pública de VagaChatVITA para PlayStation Vita.

## Novedades

- Chat compatible con APIs OpenAI mediante `chat/completions`.
- Respuestas progresivas por streaming.
- Historial local de conversaciones.
- Biblioteca de juegos instalados en la Vita.
- Chats contextuales por juego con sugerencias automáticas.
- Preguntas rápidas seleccionables con pantalla táctil y botones:
- `ARRIBA/ABAJO` para navegar.
- `IZQUIERDA/DERECHA` para cambiar de pregunta.
- `CRUZ` para enviar.
- Renderizado Markdown básico en las respuestas.
- Interfaz disponible en español, inglés e italiano.
- Configuración web local desde Ajustes.
- Servidor web protegido por contraseña.
- API key oculta en la interfaz y sin guardarse en texto plano.
- Iconos y recursos LiveArea incluidos.
- Paquete VPK listo para VitaShell.

## Instalación

1. Descargar `VagaChatVITA.vpk`.
2. Copiarlo a la Vita mediante USB o FTP.
3. Instalarlo desde VitaShell.
4. Abrir `VagaRoute AI` desde el LiveArea.
5. Configurar el endpoint y la API key desde Ajustes o Configuración web.

## Notas

- La Vita y el PC o teléfono deben estar conectados a la misma red Wi-Fi para usar la configuración web.
- El servidor web utiliza HTTP local y debe usarse únicamente en una red de confianza.
- Esta versión es alpha y puede contener errores.
- Se recomienda realizar copias de seguridad de `ux0:data/VagaRouteAI/`.

Barony Vita v0.0.2-5.0.2

v0.0.2-5.0.2 2026-09-05 19:58 UTC
# Barony Vita v0.0.2

Online multiplayer, a global leaderboard, achievements, and a batch of fixes.

## Online multiplayer
- Host or join games over the internet through the community master server, with
automatic NAT traversal and a relay fallback when a direct connection fails.
- Local ad-hoc play, and LAN over Wi-Fi, no router or internet needed.
- Set a room password when hosting.
- In-progress online games are saved for the next time your party plays together.

## Global leaderboard
- A worldwide board tied to your console, username set via settings page.
- Your best run is submitted when you open the board, whether it came from
single-player, an online game, or a save you are still playing.
- Shows the top 20, and adds your own row at the bottom with your real rank
when you are not in the top 20.
- Every entry carries the full run: class, stats, cause of death, and the
character's gear.

## Online account
- Your online identity and leaderboard progress live in one key file on the
console: ux0:data/Barony/config/gossip_id.json.
- Updating the game keeps it. Installing a newer VPK over your current install
does not touch ux0:data/Barony, so your account, saves, and leaderboard entry
all carry over.
- Deleting that file, or wiping the game's save data, permanently unlinks your
online account and its leaderboard entry. It cannot be recovered.
- A fresh account is created automatically the next time you launch, and you
set your name again. Reusing your old name may show as name#2, since the
orphaned entry still holds the original.

## Achievements
- Achievements now track and unlock during play, saved on the console and online.

## Fixes
- Lighting: removed the rainbow specks along shadow edges, lifted
pitch-black shadows so you can see in the dark (gamma slider), and smoothed the fade-to-black
banding.
- Enemies roam, infight, and give chase again instead of freezing at a distance.
This also fixes bosses appearing without their body parts.
- Torches and flames no longer drift or jitter.
- Digging or breaking a wall no longer leaves a see-through gap.
- Better handling when the console sleeps and wakes during a game.
- Stability fixes across the math and lighting code.

## Install
- Download barony-blank.vpk and install it with VitaShell.
- Barony's game files are not redistributable, so generate your own data from a
PC copy and copy it to ux0:data/Barony on the Vita. See the README for the
one-step tool.
- Cross-play with PC is not supported. Play Vita to Vita.

Built from Barony 5.0.2. GPLv3.

GITHUB · MetalSyntax/prince-of-persia-classic-psvita-port

Prince of Persia Classic — PS Vita Port v01.28 - Full Control

v01.28 2026-09-03 02:52 UTC
### Download & install

1. Download **`popclassic.vpk`** from this release's assets.
2. Install it with **VitaShell** on your PS Vita (running HENkaku/h-encore).
3. Copy the game data to `ux0:data/popclassic/` from your **legally owned** copy of the Android game.
Full guide: [INSTALL_HARDWARE.md](https://github.com/MetalSyntax/prince-of-persia-classic-psvita-port/blob/master/Docs/en/INSTALL_HARDWARE.md)

**Upgrading?** Same `TITLEID` (`POPC00001`) as every build since v01.10: **installing over an older one keeps
your saves.** Coming from v01.20 or later, just install the `.vpk` — the data in `ux0:data/popclassic/` is
unchanged.

> This repo contains **no** original game code, binaries or assets. Prince of Persia Classic is the
> intellectual property of Ubisoft Entertainment; you need your own legal copy of the Android game.

### Controls

The game switches between "platform" and "combat" mode on its own (sword drawn or not), so several buttons
do double duty.

| Button | Platform mode | Combat mode |
|:---:|:---|:---|
| **Left stick / D-Pad** | Move — tap for one careful step, **hold to run** | same |
| **Cross** | **Jump** | Attack |
| **Square** | Crouch | **Defend / parry** |
| **Triangle** | Interact (grab, levers) | Sheath sword |
| **Circle / Down** | Crouch | — |
| **Up** | Jump / climb | — |
| **Start** | Pause menu | Pause menu |
| **Select** | Menu | Menu |
| **L + R together** | Show/hide the on-screen touch buttons | same |
| **Touchscreen** | Still works for menu navigation | — |

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Coming from v01.20 or earlier, two things changed:**
> 1. **Square is no longer the "walk" modifier** — it's crouch / defend now. Walking needs no modifier any
> more: tap for a step, hold to run.
> 2. **The D-Pad runs now.** "D-Pad only walks, use the analog stick until it's fixed" was a known
> limitation from the very first build. It no longer applies.

### What's new

#### 🎮 Controls

- **You can jump while running.** This was the reported bug that survived four attempted fixes. It was never
an engine block: the synthetic-touch emulation couldn't express "run" and "jump" at once because they
competed for finite touch slots.
- **Physical buttons use the game's own gamepad path.** This port wraps the **Xperia PLAY** build, which
ships full physical-gamepad support — and the port had never switched it on (it passed `"PSVita"` as the
device name instead of `"R800i"`, the Xperia PLAY's model number, since its first commit). Now it does:
the touch buttons are hidden by the game's own code, menus get a D-Pad-navigable cursor, and tutorials
describe physical buttons.
- **Walk vs. run uses the game's real rule** (a 250 ms threshold), instead of the three invented mechanics
tried before — distance-from-centre, double-tap, drag simulation — none of which worked.
- **Cross jumps again.** v01.26 had concluded, with two functions inverted, that jump was
`control1Clicked` — which is actually *crouch*.
- **Cross confirms in menus again**, broken by the previous draft for as long as a game was loaded.
- **L+R toggle to hide the touch buttons**, now without v01.25's bug that disabled walking.
- **Memory corruption fixed**: the previous toggle wrote up to ~150 bytes past the end of an object every
time it was used.

#### 🩺 Diagnostics & stability

- **Live logs over Wi-Fi** (UDP broadcast alongside the file): a session that ends in a crash or hard reset
no longer loses its tail. `ENABLE_VERBOSE_LOG=ON` builds only.
- **Crash fixed** when starting that network logger (the `SceNet`/`SceNetCtl` modules weren't being loaded).
- **vitaGL splashscreen can be disabled** (`NO_SPLASHSCREEN`, on by default).

### Still open

- **This release is untested on console.** Most likely to need tuning: the 250 ms walk-to-run threshold.
- **Not compatible with Vita3K** — an emulator bug, not a port bug (non-power-of-2 swizzled textures). This
port targets real hardware.
- **Not using the game's original fonts**: DejaVu Serif is used instead, for licensing reasons.

---

## 🔗 Links

- **Full technical changelog** (per-version, bilingual): [Docs/CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/MetalSyntax/prince-of-persia-classic-psvita-port/blob/master/Docs/CHANGELOG.md)
- **Deep dive per fix**, with addresses and evidence: [Docs/Fixes_Log.md](https://github.com/MetalSyntax/prince-of-persia-classic-psvita-port/blob/master/Docs/Fixes_Log.md) §20–§27
- **Controls reference** for developers (`ControlsLayer` member layout, keycode → handler → event table, the `CONTROL_EVENT` bitmask, the walk→run rule): [docs/comments/main.c.md](https://github.com/MetalSyntax/prince-of-persia-classic-psvita-port/blob/master/Docs/comments/main.c.md)

GITHUB · FridiNaTor1/HPL2-handyman

Vita 1.5 and Android Vulkan 1.1

1.5 2026-09-01 21:53 UTC
Hi everyone! Big update here, since I got my SD2Vita I have been doing a lot of optimization.
I bumped the resolution of the Vita port to 480x272, so it is just a little bit more clearer, the HUD will always be Native resolution, so it doesn't become blurry.
I added a optimizer, that let's you cache the textures before hand, which improves loading times substantially, this can be skipped, and only needs to be done once!
I have made a lot of optimizations with the frame rate, and stutters. I will admit that the game is not smooth 30fps all the way through, but it is much better than it was at last release! Notable, audio, like the thunder, doesn't freeze the game for a good second, which you would notice right away at the start of the game, that is NO MORE.
There is still quite a bit of work that could be done, and I wouldn't mind if anyone would like to contribute, feel free to make pull requests. I also added a updater for the Vita, which should check on startup if you have internet, if there is a new update, you can skip it if you like, it might need more testing and refining though.

QoL improvement, I have added Hint sizes, I noticed while testing a bit, I felt the hints could be a bit hard to read at it's original size, so I have added Hint sizes, this can be changed in the gameplay options, for the Vita it's default on Medium.

I have also made the port more accessible on Android, no longer requiring Vulkan 1.3, should work on Android devices that support Vulkan 1.1+

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/FridiNaTor1/HPL2-handyman/compare/1.3...1.5

Planned features:
Controller detection for Android and PC, where the controller glyphs change depending on which type of Controller you are using, automatically, and getting rid of Controller hints when you are using Keyboard and Mouse only!
Improving the Vita control scheme, there is a part of the game where you should be using the directional button to do a puzzle, which is currently mapped incorrectly, sorry!
Improving the Android control scheme, and make it aware of desktop mode, as in when you connect the phone to a TV, the game should take advantage of that, and remove the touch only control scheme, and be able to be played with Mouse and Keyboard, or a Controller.
Better options for every platform, like keybinds/sensitivity, etc.

Known Issues:
Android stutters, this will be looked into!
Vita unstable FPS, yeah obviously, but it's a bit better now atleast!
Android running is awkward, I'll try to make it better!
Vita's inventory, pause menu, and journal, doesn't fade the background.

1.4 (PS Vita port)

1.4 2026-08-31 17:23 UTC
1.4 build of the PS Vita port (SSB64VITA).

## Changelog since 1.3

### Hi-res texture packs (new on Vita)
- Texture-pack support now works on the Vita, same model as desktop/Android: extract a pack `.zip` into `ux0:data/battleship/mods/` and it's read in place.
- Vita decode path uses **libpng** straight into the texture cache (much faster than stb_image on the Vita CPU).
- Vita-tuned memory limits: 32 MB decoded-texture LRU cache (`gHiResTextures.CacheBudgetMB` overrides), and a 1024×1024 per-texture cap — anything bigger transparently falls back to the native texture so one oversized upscale can't blow the budget.
- Directory scan uses `sceIoDread` directly instead of `std::filesystem` (which returned `EINVAL` on some valid `ux0:` pack paths and aborted the whole scan).

### Bundled texture packs
Three memory-tuned downscales of GhostlyDark's **SSB Reloaded** pack are attached to this release (and kept in-repo under `mods/texture_pack/`). Pick **one** and copy it, still zipped, to `ux0:data/battleship/mods/`:

| Pack | Scale | Notes |
|------|-------|-------|
| `texture_pack_1x.zip` | 1× | lightest; only a marginal step up from native — not really worth it |
| `texture_pack_1.5x.zip` | 1.5× | **recommended** — sharper textures, no performance hit |
| `texture_pack_2x.zip` | 2× | sharpest, but visibly slows the system; only if you accept the frame-rate cost |

Don't drop more than one in at once — every pack in `mods/` is indexed and the last one scanned wins each texture, wasting memory.

### Modding
- Mod ABI **v9**: new `fighter_special_hi_map(fighter_gobj, landing_lag)` entry point — a generalized Mario-style special-up collision/cliff path so native fighter mods can supply their own landing lag while the host keeps collision and engine-transition ownership.

### Netplay
- Build id → **1.4**. 1.4 clients only match other 1.4 clients; if you self-host the lobby board (`server/matchmaker/`), redeploy it — its default `-build` is now `1.4`.

Full details: [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/robin994/battleship-vita/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)

## Requires
- Your own copy of Super Smash Bros. (N64) US NTSC v1.0.
- `BattleShip.o2r` extracted from your ROM, copied to `ux0:data/battleship/BattleShip.o2r` (see `scripts/extract-vita-data.sh`).

## Install
Copy `battleship.vpk` to the Vita and install with VitaShell (or similar). First launch needs a few minutes to compile the shader cache — don't interrupt it.

## Known gaps
- 3–4 player netplay is not fully tested.
- A console behind CGNAT (some fibre / mobile) can only **join**, not host — no relay yet.

BombSquad Vita Alpha 0.8 fixes the clean-install data layout used by the Windows setup helper

### Downloads

- Recommended Windows setup: download `BombSquad-Vita-Alpha-0.8-Windows-Installer.zip`. It already contains the Alpha 0.8 VPK and helper. Extract it to a local Windows drive, put your exact official BombSquad Android Generic 1.7.62 APK in `install/APK PUT HERE`, then double-click `install/Install BombSquad Vita.bat`
- Manual setup: download `BombSquad-Vita-Alpha-0.8.vpk` and follow the [current installation guide](https://gitlab.com/sexcurrybeats/bombsquad-vita/-/blob/main/docs/INSTALLING.md)

You do not need the Alpha 0.7 ZIP

### Highlights

- Correctly prepares game assets under `ux0:data/bombsquad/no_backup/ballistica_files`
- Includes guided Windows preparation with optional VitaShell FTP transfer
- Includes clear manual VitaShell USB and FTP transfer instructions
- Uses the accepted renderer layout cache build and Alpha 0.8 LiveArea artwork

The project does not include the Android APK, `libmain.so`, user profiles, credentials, saves, or game assets

### Updating from Alpha 0.7

Installing only the Alpha 0.8 VPK does not correct data created by the Alpha 0.7 Windows helper

- To keep existing data, move `ux0:data/bombsquad/files` to `ux0:data/bombsquad/no_backup/ballistica_files`. The final folder must directly contain `ba_data`, `pylib`, and `payload_info`
- For a clean update, back up or rename `ux0:data/bombsquad`, install the Alpha 0.8 VPK, then run the Alpha 0.8 helper and transfer its newly prepared data folder
- If the assets were already moved to the correct path, only the Alpha 0.8 VPK update is needed

### Known issues

- Five or more active characters can cause severe frame-rate drops depending on the map and character mix
- A fresh installation can remain black for several minutes on first launch while runtime caches are created
- Initial gameplay may stutter while additional assets are cached

# Changelog

All notable changes to vitastremio (PS Vita Stremio client + middleware).

## [1.3] - 2026-08-27

**Update both halves.** Reinstall the VPK *and* restart the middleware.

### Fixed

**Sound and picture drifting apart after about 35 minutes.** Long films would
play perfectly and then, always at roughly the same point, the picture would
jump ahead of the sound and never settle again. The app was losing track of
time once playback passed 35 minutes and 47 seconds, which is why it happened
at the same moment every time. It now keeps time correctly for far longer
than any film.

### Added

**A proper loading screen.** Starting something used to show a black screen
while it buffered, which was hard to tell apart from the app having frozen.
You now get the film's artwork, its title, and a spinner while it gets ready.

### Worth knowing

- Artwork comes from your addons, so titles without it will show the title on
a plain background instead. Nothing else changes.

# FileManager Vita v0.6.2

This release focuses on stability, touch input and visual refinements.

## Highlights

- Added two color themes: **Dark**, with a black and dark-gray palette, and **Pink**, with hot-pink and light tones.
- Refined **Grid view** with the standard font size, centered file/folder names and width-aware ellipsis for long names.
- The dedicated **Icons** set is now always active and its redundant selector was removed from Settings.
- Added Wi-Fi and Bluetooth status icons. They are shown only when the corresponding connection/feature is active.
- Added touch input to controls that previously only displayed a button hint, including the **OK** button in file properties.
- Single-item copy, move and delete dialogs now show the selected file/folder name; multi-item actions retain the compact count summary.

## Stability fixes

- Limited and periodically cleaned the Recent directory, removing stale entries to prevent excessive directory growth.
- Added a five-second directory-read safeguard that returns to the default root when a directory stalls.
- Fixed IME lifecycle and buffer handling issues that could crash rename/input operations.
- Hardened VPK installation and progress-thread synchronization to prevent stalls around extraction and promotion.
- Removed the GIF background from the VPK after identifying excessive decoded-frame memory use as a potential source of freezes during installation.
- Fixed invalid touch routing while modal dialogs are open and other crash-prone edge cases found in collected logs.

## Installation

Copy `FileManager_v0.6.2.vpk` to your PS Vita and install it with VitaShell or another VPK installer. HENkaku/h-encore is required.

release-1.0.1 2026-08-27 10:51 UTC
# JAVITA 1.0.1

Bug-fix release. Install the new VPK over 1.0.0; settings, saves and texture cache are kept.

## Fixed

- **Fog.** Fog now fades out gradually instead of ending at a hard edge, and everything
drawn is affected by it, including the batched world geometry that previously ignored it.
On Hoth the render distance cut no longer shows as a dark band behind the fog.
- **Frozen mission select.** The tier menu showed a stuck frame while it compressed its
planet art on the first visit. It now shows a loading screen. The wait itself is
unchanged — see Known issues.
- **Menu characters.** Models shown on the debrief and saber screens were being folded
into the world geometry batch, which is not valid for a menu and could draw them wrong.

## Known issues

- The first visit to each tier menu is slow while its art is compressed and cached.
- Changing texture detail (`r_picmip`) discards the texture cache, so the loads after it
are slow once per area.
- Mirrors and portals draw unclipped.
- Dynamic glow is unavailable.

## Source

GPLv2 — full source for this build: https://github.com/NDRWhun/JAVITA

# ⚔️ Immortal Dusk — PS Vita Port v1.0

First official release of **Immortal Dusk** for the PlayStation Vita and PlayStation TV!

This port brings Gamevil's classic action RPG to the PS Vita natively via dynamic ARM shared library loading (`.so loader`), `FalsoJNI`, and `vitaGL` hardware scaling.

---

## ✨ Features & Highlights

- **🚀 Native 60 FPS Performance:** Internal 800x480 RGB565 software rasterizer hardware-scaled to full screen (**960x544**) with bilinear filtering via `vitaGL`.
- **🎮 Full Physical & Touch Controls:** Complete dual-input support:
- 8-direction movement via **Left Analog Stick** and **D-Pad**.
- Face buttons and triggers mapped for fast combat, skills, and item shortcuts.
- Full **Front Touchscreen** support for menus, inventory, and HUD navigation.
- **🔊 Low-Latency Multi-Voice Audio Engine:** Powered by `sceAudioOut`, supporting 12-voice polyphonic WAV PCM sound effects and memory-streamed looping MP3 background music (`minimp3`).
- **💎 Offline Cash Shop & K-Point Emulation:** Built-in local simulation of Gamevil's legacy server protocol, preventing infinite loading hangs and allowing purchases of potions, resurrection stones, teleport scrolls, and bag/storage expansions completely offline.
- **🖼️ High-Quality LiveArea:** Custom icon, startup gate, and background remastered with 8-bit indexed palettes matching PS Vita OS standards.

---

## 🕹️ Controls

| PS Vita Button | In-Game Action |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Left Stick / D-Pad** | 8-Direction Character Movement |
| **Cross ($\times$)** | Primary Attack / Talk / Confirm |
| **Square ($\square$)** | Skill 1 |
| **Triangle ($\triangle$)** | Skill 2 |
| **Circle ($\bigcirc$)** | Skill 3 / Cancel / Back |
| **R1 Trigger** | Skill 4 |
| **L1 Trigger** | Quick HP Potion |
| **SELECT** | Quick MP Potion |
| **START** | In-Game Menu / Pause |
| **Front Touchscreen** | Direct touch interaction across menus, inventory, and HUD |

---

## 📦 Requirements & Installation Guide

> **Legal Disclaimer:** This release only provides the loader executable (`.vpk`). No copyrighted assets or proprietary binaries are included. You must supply files from a legally acquired copy of **Immortal Dusk v1.0.2** for Android.

### 1. Prerequisites on your PS Vita
Ensure you have the following plugins installed:
- [kubridge.skprx](https://github.com/TheOfficialFloW/kubridge/releases)
- [fd_fix.skprx](https://github.com/TheOfficialFloW/FdFix/releases) (or rePatch)
- `libshacccg.suprx` (installed in `ur0:data/` via *ShaRKBR3ED* or *CrystalPSM*)

---

### 2. Setup Steps
1. Download and install **`immortal_dusk.vpk`** on your PS Vita using **VitaShell**.
2. Obtain your legal **`Immortal Dusk_1.0.2.apk`** file and rename/extract it as a `.zip` archive.
3. Extract and copy the following files to `ux0:data/immortaldusk/`:
- Copy `lib/armeabi/libaist-jni.so` $\to$ `ux0:data/immortaldusk/libaist-jni.so`
- Copy the APK's `assets/` folder $\to$ `ux0:data/immortaldusk/assets/`
- Copy the APK's `res/raw/` folder $\to$ `ux0:data/immortaldusk/res/raw/`

#### 📂 Final Folder Structure on `ux0:`
```text
ux0:data/immortaldusk/
├── libaist-jni.so
├── assets/
│ ├── ani_data/
│ ├── data/
│ ├── font/
│ ├── img/
│ ├── txt/
│ └── txte/
├── res/
│ └── raw/
│ ├── snd0.wav ... snd61.wav
│ └── snd100.mp3 ... snd122.mp3
└── saves/
```

4. Launch the game from your LiveArea and enjoy!

---

- **Rinnegatamante** for `vitaGL` and invaluable contributions to the PS Vita scene.
- **Volodymyr Atamanenko** for `so_util` and soloader boilerplate.

# DESTINIA (PS Vita / PSTV) — Release v1.0.0

Native ARM loader and port of Gamevil's classic Action-RPG **DESTINIA** (데스티니아) for PlayStation Vita and PlayStation TV.

---

## 🌟 Features

- **🎮 Full Physical Controls:** Seamless control mapping for D-Pad, Left Analog Stick, Face Buttons, Triggers, and Menu navigation.
- **🎨 Hardware Visual Enhancements & Filters:**
- **Sharp Pixel-Art 2x (Default):** Crisp, pixel-perfect rendering without distortion or shimmering.
- **Smooth Bilinear 2x:** Smooth sub-pixel blending for players who prefer filtered visuals.
- **Vibrant OLED / LCD Mode:** Brightness, contrast, and saturation boost (+15%) tailored for both PS Vita 1000 (OLED) and 2000 (LCD) screens.
- **Aspect Ratio Selector:** Native 5:3 Fit (`906x544`), Integer 2x Center (`800x480`), and Fullscreen 16:9 (`960x544`).
- **On-the-Fly Hotkeys:** Cycle filters (`L1 + R1 + △`) and aspect ratios (`L1 + R1 + ▢`) during gameplay with automatic config saving.
- **🔊 High-Fidelity Audio:** Multi-channel Vorbis (`Tremor`) audio engine supporting looping background music (`BGM`) and simultaneous sound effects (`SFX`).
- **⚡ Rock-Solid 60 FPS Native Execution:** Direct execution on ARM Cortex-A9 CPU with GPU hardware-accelerated rasterization (via `vitaGL`).
- **🛡️ Anti-DMCA Compliant:** Clean data extraction scripts to extract assets from your legally acquired Android APK.

---

## 🎮 Controls

| Action | PS Vita Input |
|---|---|
| **Movement / Direction** | **D-Pad** or **Left Analog Stick** |
| **Attack / Confirm** | **Cross (✕)** or **Circle (○)** |
| **Skill Slot 1** | **Square (□)** |
| **Skill Slot 2** | **Triangle (△)** |
| **Skill Slot 3** | **R1 Trigger** |
| **Quick Potion / Slot 1** | **L1 Trigger** |
| **Main Menu / Back** | **Start** |
| **Status / Map** | **Select** |
| **Cycle Graphics Filter** | **L1 + R1 + Triangle (△)** |
| **Cycle Aspect Ratio** | **L1 + R1 + Square (□)** |
| **Touch Controls** | **Front Touch Screen** |

---

## 📥 Installation Instructions

### Prerequisites
1. PlayStation Vita with Henkaku / Enso CFW.
2. [**kubridge.skprx**](https://github.com/TheOfficialFloW/FdFmx/releases) (v0.2 or newer) installed in `ur0:tai/config.txt`.
3. [**libshacccg.suprx**](https://github.com/SKGleba/ShaRKBR33D) extracted.

### Setup Steps
1. Install **`destinia_enhanced.vpk`** (or `destinia.vpk`) using **VitaShell**.
2. Obtain the Android APK file for **DESTINIA v1.0.6** (Package: `game.destiniaeng`).
3. Extract the assets using the included PC script:
```bash
./porting_tools/prepare_data_files.sh /path/to/destinia-1-0-6.apk
```
Or manually place the game files into:
- `ux0:data/destinia/libdestinia_jni.so`
- `ux0:data/destinia/assets/`
- `ux0:data/destinia/sound/`
4. Launch **DESTINIA** from your LiveArea!

---

## 🛠️ Technical Changelog

- **FalsoJNI Heap Architecture Refactoring:** Fixed pointer invalidation on internal dynamic array reallocations (`JavaDynArray**`), preventing Data Abort crashes during asset loading and combat events.
- **Memory Optimization:** Added automatic buffer recycling for resource loaders (`Java_getAssetRes`), eliminating memory leaks during map transitions.
- **Crash-Proof Hardware Pipeline:** Switched from unstable runtime shader translation to a dedicated hardware-accelerated rendering pipeline in `vitaGL`.
- **Automatic Cache Maintenance:** Added early purging for corrupted `.gxp` cache files.

---

- **Rinnegatamante** for [vitaGL](https://github.com/Rinnegatamante/vitaGL).
- **TheFloW** for [kubridge](https://github.com/TheOfficialFloW/FdFmx) and soloader foundation.
- **Volodymyr Atamanenko** and **Andy Nguyen** for [FalsoJNI](https://github.com/v-atamanenko/falsojni).

Cordless v1.0.0

v1.0.0 2026-08-20 03:07 UTC
# Cordless 1.0.0

A native Discord client for the PlayStation Vita. It talks straight to Discord over TLS, so there's no bridge server and nothing to self-host.

## Features
- Servers, DMs, group DMs, and threads
- Send, edit, reply, react, and forward; scroll up to load history
- Images, GIFs, WebP, and video / voice-message playback
- Emoji, live presence, typing indicators, friends, and profile popouts
- Join by invite, block users, and multiple accounts
- Settings: light/dark theme, accent color, font size, compact mode, 12/24h clock, and a low-battery mode

Voice channels are still a work in progress and are turned off in this build.

## Logging in
No password either way. Two options:

- QR code: scan the on-screen code with the official Discord mobile app. It's the quick path, but Discord sometimes asks for a captcha during QR sign-in that the Vita can't complete. If that happens, use the token method.
- Token: put your Discord user token on the card once. The full walkthrough (a one-click bookmarklet, the browser Network tab, or by hand) is in docs/login.md. (https://github.com/Brendonm17/Cordless/blob/main/docs/login.md)

## Terms of service
Using a user token with a third-party client is against Discord's Terms of Service. Cordless is built for personal use and interoperability, not automation, and you run it on your own account at your own risk. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by Discord or Sony.

AI was used for API research and live area assets.

## Install
1. A Vita or PS TV on HENkaku / h-encore2 (firmware 3.60 to 3.74) with unsafe homebrew enabled.
2. Copy Cordless.vpk to the Vita and install it in VitaShell.
3. Launch it, then follow docs/login.md to add your token.

Logs are written to ux0:data/cordless/log.txt.

VitaBrightEX v1.3 + LUT Editor v4.2

v1.3 2026-08-18 09:10 UTC
## VitaBrightEX v1.3 + LUT Editor v4.2

### Critical fixes in this release

**OLED: presets no longer destroy screen colours**

The previous OLED screen filter applied CCT/gamma/contrast math directly
to the panel's 21-byte LUT rows. Those bytes are panel hardware control
registers — not linear RGB pixel values. Applying a colour matrix to them
produced wrong results and made every single preset look worse than the
default. This is now fully fixed.

The OLED LUT is left completely untouched by the filter system. Your
screen colour is set by the calibrated per-panel LUT file
(vitabright_lut_p5.txt etc.) loaded at boot — which already has the
correct white-point for your specific panel. Factory reset restores
this clean state instantly.

**Tab switching now works reliably**

The app was using sceCtrlPeekBufferPositiveExt2 which remaps the
physical L/R shoulder buttons to different bit positions (L1/R1 DS4
style) that the code wasn't reading. Fixed: uses plain
sceCtrlPeekBufferPositive so the physical L/R buttons correctly
switch tabs.

---

### What each part now does

**Plugin v1.3**
- OLED colour is controlled by the per-panel LUT file only
- Filter math (CCT/gamma/contrast) is NOT applied to OLED — it was
the wrong architecture and destroyed calibration
- Hardware invert (sceDisplaySetInvertColorsForDriver) still works
- LCD filter (IFTU CSC matrix) unchanged — works correctly

**App v4.2 on Vita 1000 (OLED):**
- Tab 1: Invert toggle + Factory reset — the only safe options
- Tab 2: Invert only, with explanation of why CCT/gamma/contrast
are not shown (to prevent accidentally breaking colours)

**App v4.2 on Vita 2000 (LCD):**
- Tab 1: Full CCT preset list (6500K–1200K) + IPS/sRGB/Night/Boost
enhancements — correct because IFTU CSC applies to pixel data
- Tab 2: Temperature / Gamma / Contrast / Brightness / Invert sliders

**Factory reset (Triangle):** Calls vitabrightOledReload() to restore
the clean panel LUT from the panel-specific file on disk, then clears
invert. Restores original colours immediately without a reboot.

---

### Installation
1. Extract VitaBrightEX-v1.3.zip and copy all files to ur0:/tai/
2. Add ur0:/tai/vitabright.skprx under *KERNEL in ur0:/tai/config.txt
3. Reboot
4. Install VitaBrightEX-LUT-Editor-v4.2.vpk via VitaShell

If ux0:/tai/ exists on your memory card it takes priority over ur0:/tai/.

---

Based on vitabright by devnoname120 (https://github.com/devnoname120/vitabright).
Screen filter inspired by Luma3DS Rosalina (https://github.com/LumaTeam/Luma3DS).

## ⚔️ Zenonia 4 — PlayStation Vita Port (v1.0.0)

First official release of the native **Zenonia 4 (Android)** port for the **PlayStation Vita**, featuring **intelligent multi-tier FrameSkip**, **direct RGB565 hardware rendering**, **RAM audio caching**, and **maximum CPU optimization**.

---

## 🚀 What's New in v1.0.0

- **⚡ Multi-Tier FrameSkip (1.0x to 3.0x)**:
- Dynamic frame pacing allowing you to adjust game speed in real-time between **1.0x (Normal)**, **1.5x**, **2.0x (Default)**, **2.5x**, and **3.0x (Max)**.
- Game logic, physics, enemy AI, and touch/pad inputs run at a full **60 Hz tick rate** while rendering load is cut down, yielding a super-smooth 20–30+ FPS experience.
- Frame pacing is active across gameplay, Title screen animations, and Main Menus.
- **🖥️ On-Screen OSD HUD Notification**:
- Displays a clean, translucent banner at the top of the screen when changing speed modes (`FRAME SKIP: 2.0X`, etc.) with smooth fade-out.
- **🛡️ 100% Authentic Visuals & UI Bug Fixes**:
- Off-screen text and button caches (`p9 != 0`) are fully preserved, fixing missing text labels on pause/inventory popups (*Destroy*, *Repair*, *Equip*, *Discard*).
- Redundant 1.04 MB `FastClearNonClipping` writes are bypassed on skipped frames to drastically reduce RAM bandwidth usage.
- **🔇 Zero-Log Max CPU Performance**:
- Release binaries are built with file logging disabled (`ENABLE_LOGGING=OFF`), eliminating SD card / SD2Vita write latency and format-string overhead during gameplay.
- **🎵 Multi-Core Thread Affinity**:
- Main game loop pinned to **CPU Core 0** at 444 MHz.
- Audio mixing and background OGG playback isolated to **CPU Core 1** with zero SD card access (audio cached in RAM).

---

| **START + SELECT** | Exit Game safely |
| **Front Touchscreen** | Full native touch controls & menu navigation |

---

## 📦 Installation Instructions

1. Install `zenonia_4.vpk` on your PlayStation Vita via **VitaShell**.
2. Extract the game asset files from the Android APK (`assets/` and `lib/armeabi/libgameDSO.so`) into `ux0:data/zenonia-4/`.
3. Ensure `ux0:data/zenonia-4/libgameDSO.so` and `ux0:data/zenonia-4/assets/` are present.
4. Launch **Zenonia 4** from LiveArea and enjoy the game!

---

v1.11 2026-08-12 11:39 UTC
## MCSM 1.11 — public prerelease

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **This is a fix pass, not a confirmed-working pass.** Everything below was
> traced from code, disassembly, or a device `loader.log` and fixed on that
> basis — none of it has been confirmed by a full playthrough yet. In
> particular, this release does **not** claim choices or settings now save
> correctly; it describes the specific mechanisms that were found broken and
> what changed. If a problem persists, the logging build exists to find out
> why instead of guessing again.
>
> **The VPK on this release is a LOGGING build (`MCSM-1.11-logging.vpk`).**
> It writes a diagnostic log to `ux0:data/mcsm/loader.log` while you play,
> and it runs slower than a normal build because of it — please don't report
> its framerate as a performance bug. A non-logging build
> (`MCSM-1.11.vpk`) is also attached.
>
> ### How to send a log
>
> 1. Play until the problem happens.
> 2. Close the game. If it is frozen: press **PS**, then close it from the LiveArea.
> 3. **Do not launch the game again yet** — the log is wiped at the start of every
> launch, so relaunching destroys what you just captured.
> 4. Copy `ux0:data/mcsm/loader.log` off the Vita — open VitaShell, press **SELECT**
> to start its FTP server, and copy the file from a PC.
> 5. Attach it to a [bug report](../../issues/new?template=bug-report.yml) or post it
> in the [Discord](https://discord.gg/spjFgQUGmE). Zip it if it is large.
>
> To turn logging off without changing builds, create an empty
> `ux0:data/mcsm/settings/nolog.txt`.

> **Use Data Builder v1.9** (unchanged from 1.10 — same file, reused as-is).

This release contains the PS Vita loader with community LiveArea artwork and trophy support, the Windows data builder, and the corresponding source code. It does **not** contain the Android APK, OBBs, episodes, native game libraries, or gameplay archives.

Questions, test results, and bug reports are welcome in the [MCSM Vita Discord](https://discord.gg/spjFgQUGmE).

### Downloads

- **MCSM-1.11-logging.vpk** — complete Vita loader, **logging build** (see the box above); install with VitaShell.
- **MCSM-1.11.vpk** — the same loader without logging, for normal play once a problem is no longer being chased.
- **MCSM-Vita-Data-Builder-v1.9.exe** — unchanged from 1.10; builds `ux0:data/mcsm` or a chapter-only copy pack from your legally owned Android files.

### What changed in this pass

- **Preference load ran before its resource could exist.** `SavePrefs` was writing correctly the whole time; the load that reads it back now retries once the resource it needs is actually registered, instead of only trying once, too early, at boot.
- **Found and fixed a real bug in the shipped engine's event log**, not a porting artifact: on a missing anchor event, `DeleteAllEventsAfterEvent` underflows to a full-log wipe instead of doing nothing. `SaveLoad_Load` calls the vulnerable path on every load; it's now guarded against exactly that case.
- **The post-save mirror was guessing which copy the engine wrote, and guessed wrong** — from the second save onward it silently overwrote every save with the first one's contents. It now checks which copy actually changed instead of assuming.
- Save writes are now staged and size-verified before being committed by rename, and a one-generation backup restores a save that's provably too small to be intact.
- **Audio mixer was writing into a buffer the hardware was still playing**, audible as tearing in busy scenes with several NPCs on screen; it now rotates through buffers that were already allocated but unused.
- **The virtual controller could be dropped by the system around common dialogs** (trophy setup, the rename keyboard) and never came back, leaving only touch controls; it's now checked and re-added automatically.
- **The 30fps cap allowed a fast frame through right after a slow one**; presents are now floored against the actual previous present so the display can't exceed the configured cap.
- **An animation-timing repair forced a quarter-second jump on every scene load**, not just on the hitches it was meant to smooth; it now treats a load as a pause (nothing to catch up to) rather than lost time.
- The save-rename on-screen keyboard could show leftover characters from a previous rename on top of the new one; its input buffer is now cleared between uses.
- New LiveArea icon and content-screen artwork.

### Data Builder v1.9

Unchanged from the 1.10 release.
